sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Core Philosophy**: Emphasized the worship of **Nirankar** (the Formless God), rejecting idol worship and ritualistic practices that had crept into Sikhism.
• **Institutional Focus**: Advocated for **Anand Karaj** (Sikh marriage ceremony) to be performed in the presence of the Guru Granth Sahib, moving away from Vedic rites.
• **Social Reform**: Opposed the caste system, dowry, and extravagant funeral rites, promoting simplicity and equality.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The movement acted as a **puritanical revivalist force** that sought to define 'Sikh' identity distinctly from 'Hindu' identity during the early British colonial period.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Centered in Rawalpindi (now in Pakistan); focused on 'Nirankar' (Formless).
Reaction against the influence of Brahmanical rituals in Sikh Gurdwaras.
Prelims: Distinguish from the later 'Sant Nirankari' sect (post-1929).
Advocated simple marriage (Anand Karaj) and rejection of caste-based discrimination.
Emphasis on the teachings of Guru Nanak Dev Ji.
Mains: Link to the broader 19th-century 'Sikh Renaissance' and identity formation.

items.definition: Literally 'Formless'. The central theological concept of Baba Dayal Das, asserting that God has no physical form, thus prohibiting idol worship.
The Sikh marriage ceremony formalized by the Nirankari movement to replace Vedic rituals, emphasizing the union of two souls in the presence of the Guru Granth Sahib.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Purification of Rituals**: Systematic removal of non-Sikh practices from life-cycle ceremonies.
• **Educational Outreach**: Use of 'Hukamnamas' (written orders) to disseminate reformist ideals among the Sikh peasantry.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Resistance from the traditional priestly class (Mahants) who benefited from ritualistic practices.
• **Solutions**: Institutionalization of the movement through the establishment of the Nirankari Darbar.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'D-A-N' (Dayal - Anand - Nirankar).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Dayal Das founded the movement, promoted Anand Karaj, and worshipped the Nirankar (Formless).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the 19th-century 'Nirankari' movement (Baba Dayal Das) with the 20th-century 'Sant Nirankari' mission (founded by Buta Singh). They are distinct entities.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Sikh Revivalism' to describe the Nirankari movement, highlighting how it provided the intellectual foundation for the later Singh Sabha Movement.

keyTakeaways: Baba Dayal Das was a pioneer of the 19th-century Sikh reform movement.
The movement was strictly monotheistic, rejecting idol worship and Brahmanical rituals.
The Nirankari movement laid the groundwork for the later Singh Sabha movement and the codification of Sikh identity.
